ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The figure below is a photomicrograph taken by a certain student while observing mitosis in onion root tip cells. Question: In cell A, at what position is the centromere of each chromosome arranged?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the photomicrograph, the cell labeled “A” is located near the upper right of the field of view. Darker chromosome structures can be seen inside the cell, appearing as short rods, and they are centrally arranged in the central region of the cell rather than dispersed to the two ends of the cell. Reasoning: The question stem states that this figure is a photomicrograph of mitosis in onion root tip cells; the chromosomes in cell A are concentrated in the center of the cell, which conforms to the typical feature of metaphase of mitosis. During metaphase of mitosis, the centromere of each chromosome is arranged on the equatorial plate in the center of the cell. Therefore, in cell A, the centromere of each chromosome is arranged on the equatorial plate.
